top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, one writer, one prize part) is preferred on literary grounds, not on the six-way convergence, which I do not count as merit. From public knowledge and translation, the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid have a voice recognisable as no one else's. Their patterned architecture is carried by the sentence as well as by scale, and memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation form one imaginative project. The work runs from poetry into long prose cycles, which supports an arc across the oeuvre rather than a single peak. The round-2 citation is narrowed to prose grounded in a poet's language, because the poetry is thinly visible in translation. Real uncertainties remain: Romanian sentence rhythm and density can be judged only through translations of uneven quality, and I cannot confirm volume by volume that later books extend rather than repeat earlier motifs. I have not independently verified any source. Even so, the case is substantive enough that P001 ranks above no award (P000). The slate holds only these two proposals, so Adonis, Can Xue and other alternatives named in round 2 are not ranked here.
recusal_note: None apparent from the profile, which records no connection to Cărtărescu. My scholarly interests (the fragment, nihilism, mysticism, modern poetry) are context only, and I have flagged the risk that I overvalue an inward, metaphysical project. As chair I also ranked B014 first myself. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
